turns.text: Turn the clock back to 1992. What problem was Williams's REINFORCE actually trying to solve?

Reinforcement-learning agents needed a direct way to improve stochastic policies from delayed rewards without differentiating through the environment. Williams developed a family of likelihood-ratio updates that became known as REINFORCE.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?

The algorithm increases the log-probability of sampled actions in proportion to the return they receive. This produces an unbiased policy-gradient estimate, although its variance can be high without baselines or other variance reduction.
Why did the idea outlive one paper or experiment? What did later researchers actually inherit?

Experts generally regard REINFORCE as the foundational Monte Carlo policy-gradient algorithm. Modern policy optimization, language-model reinforcement learning, and differentiable sampling methods still build on its score-function estimator.
Williams's REINFORCE mattered not only as a result, but as a method that later researchers could test, adapt, and extend.
